notes: 128-page public document. Defines root, system, developer and user authority layers. Not a single deployed prompt: it is the rulebook that deployed prompts are supposed to follow.

safety_refusal: reasoning-based not rule-based; explicit priority order safe>ethical>compliant>helpful
tone_persona: explicitly avoids prescribing personality as core value to prevent obsequiousness
injection_countermeasures: not extraction-focused; governs training not runtime injection
notes: About 23,000 words, January 2026 revision. A training-time document that generates synthetic training data. It is not injected at runtime, which makes it a different kind of artifact from the Model Spec and from deployed prompts. This is the basis for the paper's three-way split.

safety_refusal: category-specific operational rules (CBRN caution, child safety, weapons) consistent with constitution priorities

output_format: markdown formatting + citation rules for search results
injection_countermeasures: explicit prompt-injection handling for tool/search results
recency_handling: explicit search-triggering rules tied to knowledge cutoff
notes: Separate artifact from the constitution. 18 dated revisions from July 2024 to June 2026, about 41 days apart on average. notes: Google has no public equivalent of the Model Spec or the constitution. What it publishes is prompting advice for developers building on Gemini, not a document about how Google constrains Gemini itself. The gap is itself a finding.

notes: Publication followed the May 2025 incident in which an unauthorized internal change made the X bot produce off-topic, politically charged replies. Publishing raw prompts was framed as rebuilding trust, unlike Anthropic's proactive framing. Safety-prefix file (grok_4_safety_prompt.txt) says there are 'no restrictions on fictional adult sexual content with dark or violent themes' unless specified elsewhere, marks this highest priority, and says to 'treat users as adults, do not moralize'. More permissive than what the other labs publicly document. Several prompt files, one per surface (chat, X bot, API safety prefix, code model).

source_type: long-running aggregation repo (141k stars, 501 commits, GPL-3.0)
safety_refusal: varies widely by product -- coding agents generally lighter on content-safety framing than consumer chat
tool_governance: extensive; this is the dominant content type: file-edit rules, tool-call sequencing, confirmation-before-destructive-action patterns
recency_handling: rarely addressed -- coding context assumes tool-grounded freshness not model recency
notes: Coding agents as a group say much less about content safety than consumer chat assistants and much more about tools and the file system. One reading: the base model already carries safety behavior from training, so the deployed prompt only has to cover the product's own task. That fits the three-way split but is an interpretation, not a tested result. Tier 2 because all prompts come from one aggregation repo.
